## Question 1: Differential expression

Which genes are differentially expressed between PD cases and healthy controls? Please also visualise your DE results with appropriate plots.

### Load packages and data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(edgeR)
library(limma)
library(pheatmap)
library(ggrepel)

load("data/rnaseq.Rda")
load("data/rnaseq_gene_info.Rda")
```

### Filter out lowly expressed genes

This includes only genes with counts of at least 10 in the analysis.

```{r}
keep <- filterByExpr(dge)
table(keep)
dge <- dge[keep, , keep.lib.sizes = FALSE]
dge$samples

# Check whether the count matrix dimensions have been reduced
dim(dge$counts)
```

### Normalise raw counts

Normalisation allows samples to be compared while accounting for differences in sequencing depth and RNA composition:

- **Sequencing depth (library size, using CPM):** counts scaled to the number expected for a library of one million.
- **RNA composition:** adjusted using TMM normalisation.

```{r}
dge <- normLibSizes(dge, method = "TMM")

# View the normalisation factors
dge$samples
```

### Limma-voom framework

The limma-voom framework transforms the data to better meet the assumptions of a linear model, allowing differential expression to be identified from normalised data.

#### Fit the linear model

The design matrix represents the covariates. Here, the covariate is group (control versus case).

```{r}
design <- model.matrix(~ 0 + group, data = dge$samples)
colnames(design) <- c("Control", "Case")

# Compare controls with cases
# A positive log-fold change indicates higher expression in PD cases
contr_matrix <- makeContrasts(
  CasevsControl = "Case - Control",
  levels = design
)
```

#### Transform counts using voom

Raw RNA-seq counts are highly skewed, and their variance increases with their mean. Lowly expressed genes are proportionally noisier than highly expressed genes.

The `voom()` function converts counts to log-CPM values using the library sizes and normalisation factors calculated above. It also estimates the mean-variance relationship and assigns a precision weight to each observation. Noisier observations therefore have less influence on the linear model.

The voom plot shows the mean-variance relationship: the x-axis is average log2 expression and the y-axis is the square root of the residual standard deviation.

```{r}
v <- voom(dge, design, plot = TRUE)
```

#### Fit the model and apply contrasts

The fitted model contains coefficients representing weighted average log-CPM expression for each phenotype group. `contrasts.fit()` then calculates the specified comparison between groups.

```{r}
vfit <- lmFit(v, design)

# Check coefficients for each group
head(vfit$coefficients)

vfit <- contrasts.fit(vfit, contrasts = contr_matrix)


# Check coefficients for the contrast
head(vfit$coefficients)
```

### Test for differential expression

The `eBayes()` function computes moderated t-statistics, moderated F-statistics, and log-odds of differential expression. Empirical Bayes moderation borrows information across genes to improve estimates of variability.

```{r}

efit <- eBayes(vfit)

# Classify genes as upregulated, downregulated, or not significantly differentially expressed
dt <- decideTests(efit)
dt
summary(dt)

# Retrieve the results for the case-versus-control contrast
top <- topTable(
  efit, 
  coef = "CasevsControl", 
  n = Inf
  )
```

### Join differential-expression results with Entrez IDs

The `topTable()` output includes the log-fold change, average expression, moderated t-statistic, p-value, adjusted p-value, and log-odds of differential expression.

```{r}
top_results <- as_tibble(top)

gene_names <- entrez_genename_key %>%
 rename(genes = entrezid)

top_annotated <- left_join(top_results, gene_names, by = "genes")

de_genes <- efit$genes %>%
 rename(entrezid = genes)

de_annotated <- left_join(de_genes, entrez_genename_key, by = "entrezid")
```

### Visualise differential-expression results

A table of p-values and fold changes can be difficult to interpret, so the results are visualised using an MA plot and a volcano plot.

#### MA plot

```{r}
ma_plot_data <- tibble(
  logFC = efit$coefficients[, "CasevsControl"],
  AvgExpr = efit$Amean,
  status = factor(as.numeric(dt[, "CasevsControl"])),
  gene = de_annotated$gene_name,
  p_value = efit$p.value[, "CasevsControl"]
)

ma_plot_data_fct <- ma_plot_data %>%
  mutate(
    status = factor(
      status,
      levels = c(0, -1, 1),
      labels = c("Not DE", "Down", "Up")
    )
  )

top_de_genes <- ma_plot_data_fct %>%
  slice_min(n = 15, p_value) |>
  na.omit()

scale_cols <- c(
  "Not DE" = "#B0B0B0",  # Grey: Not significant
  "Down"   = "#0072B2",  # Blue: Downregulated in PD
  "Up"     = "#E31A1C"   # Red: Upregulated in PD
)

ggplot(ma_plot_data_fct,
       aes(x = AvgExpr, y = logFC, colour = status)) +

  # Non-significant genes (grey background)
  geom_point(
    data = ma_plot_data_fct %>%
      filter(status == "Not DE"),
    size = 0.5,
    alpha = 0.35
  ) +

  # Significant genes (red and blue)
  geom_point(
    data = ma_plot_data_fct %>%
      filter(status != "Not DE"),
    size = 2,
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +

  # Labels for top genes
  geom_label_repel(
    data = top_de_genes,
    aes(label = gene),
    colour = "black",
    size = 3,
    max.overlaps = 20,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +

  scale_colour_manual(values = scale_cols) +

  theme_classic() +

  labs(
    title = "MA Plot: Parkinson's Disease vs Control",
    x = "Average log2 expression",
    y = "Log2 fold change (PD - Control)",
    colour = "Gene expression"
  )
```

#### Volcano plot

```{r}

# Define consistent colours
scale_cols <- c(
  "Not DE" = "#B0B0B0",
  "Down"   = "#0072B2",
  "Up"     = "#E31A1C"
)

# Prepare data for plotting
volcano_data <- ma_plot_data_fct %>%
  mutate(
    FDR = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"),
    neg_log10_FDR = -log10(pmax(FDR, .Machine$double.xmin))
  )

# Select 10 significant genes for labelling
label_genes <- volcano_data %>%
  filter(status != "Not DE", !is.na(gene)) %>%
  slice_min(FDR, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE)

# Set symmetrical x-axis limits
x_limit <- ceiling(max(abs(volcano_data$logFC), na.rm = TRUE))

# Create the volcano plot
volcano_plot <- ggplot(
  volcano_data,
  aes(x = logFC, y = neg_log10_FDR, colour = status)
) +

  # Non-significant genes
  geom_point(
    data = volcano_data %>% filter(status == "Not DE"),
    size = 0.7,
    alpha = 0.35
  ) +

  # Significant genes
  geom_point(
    data = volcano_data %>% filter(status != "Not DE"),
    size = 2.5,
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +

  # Significance threshold
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = -log10(0.05),
    linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "grey40",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +

  # No-change reference line
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "grey50",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +

  # Gene labels
  geom_label_repel(
    data = label_genes,
    aes(label = gene),
    colour = "black",
    size = 3.5,
    max.overlaps = Inf,
    box.padding = 0.5,
    point.padding = 0.3,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +

  # Colours and legend
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = scale_cols,
    breaks = c("Up", "Down", "Not DE"),
    labels = c(
      "Upregulated",
      "Downregulated",
      "Not significant"
    ),
    name = "Expression status"
  ) +

  # Symmetrical x-axis
  coord_cartesian(
    xlim = c(-x_limit, x_limit)
  ) +

  # Titles and labels
  labs(
    title = "Differential Gene Expression in Parkinson's Disease",
    subtitle = "PD cases vs healthy controls (FDR < 0.05)",
    x = expression(log[2] ~ "fold change (PD vs Control)"),
    y = expression(-log[10] ~ "(FDR-adjusted p-value)")
  ) +

  theme_classic(base_size = 15) +

  theme(
    # Centre title and subtitle
   plot.title.position = "panel",
  plot.title = element_text(
    hjust = 0.5,
    size = 16,
    face = "bold"
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      hjust = 0.5,
      size = 12,
      colour = "grey40"
    ),

    # Axis labels
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),

    # Legend
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.position = "right",

    # Plot margins
    plot.margin = margin(12, 20, 12, 12)
  )

volcano_plot

```

```{r}
# Save volcano plot 
ggsave(
  filename = "volcano_plot.png",
  plot = volcano_plot,
  width = 11,
  height = 7,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)
```


## Question 2: Gene ontology

Which gene ontology families do the differentially expressed genes belong to?

```{r}
go <- gene_ontology %>%
 rename(entrezid = entrezgene_id)

go_annotated <- left_join(go, entrez_genename_key) %>%
 rename(gene = gene_name)

de_go <- left_join(top_de_genes, go_annotated)

de_go %>%
 select(gene, desc)
```

## Question 3: Sample clustering

Is the clustering of samples by gene expression consistent with their disease status as cases and controls?

### Multidimensional scaling (MDS) clustering

The MDS plot shows whether phenotype groups tend to cluster together, indicating that samples within a group have similar gene-expression profiles.

The distance between each pair of samples is calculated using the leading fold change, defined as the root-mean-square of the largest 500 log2-fold changes between that pair of samples.

If samples from the same group cluster together and samples from different groups form separate clusters, this suggests that between-group differences are larger than within-group variation.

```{r}
col.cell <- c("#E30B5C", "#800080")[dge$samples$group]

plotMDS(
  dge,
  col = col.cell,
  labels = dge$samples$group
)

legend(
  "topleft",
  fill = c("#E30B5C", "#800080"),
  legend = levels(dge$samples$group)
)
```

### Save results for collaborative analysis

```{r}
saveRDS(ma_plot_data_fct, "RNAseq_expression_status.rds")
saveRDS(go_annotated, "GO_terms.rds")
```
